subject: maths
question: In an election between two candidates 87% of the registered voters cast their vote and 5% of the votes polled were found invalid. The winning candidate got 52% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1653 votes. How many voters were registered?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total registered voters be V.

Winner gets 52% and loser gets 48% of valid votes, so the margin is 4% of valid votes.

Margin = V × Polled% × Valid% × Margin%

1653 = V × (87/100) × (95/100) × (4/100)

1653 = V × (87/100) × (19/20) × (1/25) ⇒ 1653 = V × (1653/50000) ⇒ V = 50000

**∴ The correct answer is 50000 voters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Registered (100%) = V
 
• 
 
 Polled (87%)
 
• 
 
 Valid (95% of Polled)
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Winner (52%)
 
 Loser (48%)
 

 Margin = 4% = 1653 votes

**Given:**

Total voters cast their vote = 87%

Invalid votes = 5% of polled votes

Winner's vote share = 52% of valid votes

Winning margin = 1653 votes

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total registered voters be V.

⇒ Number of polled votes = 87% of V = (87/100) × V

⇒ Since 5% are invalid, valid votes = 95% of polled votes = (95/100) × (87/100) × V = (19/20) × (87/100) × V

⇒ Loser's vote share = 100% − 52% = 48% of valid votes

⇒ Winning margin = Winner's share − Loser's share = 52% − 48% = 4% of valid votes

⇒ 4% of valid votes = (4/100) × (19/20) × (87/100) × V = (1/25) × (19/20) × (87/100) × V

⇒ Margin is 1653 votes:

⇒ (1/25) × (19/20) × (87/100) × V = 1653

⇒ (1653 / 50000) × V = 1653

⇒ V = 1653 × (50000 / 1653)

⇒ V = 50000

**∴ The correct answer is 50000 voters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Percentage Concept

In election problems, valid votes are always calculated from polled votes, and the winning margin is strictly the difference between the percentages of the candidates based on valid votes.

Successive Percentage

Reductions in an election (voters who did not vote, invalid votes) can be calculated successively as continuous fraction multiplications: Base × (100 − x)% × (100 − y)%.

Margin of Victory Formula

Margin of Victory = Votes of Winner − Votes of Loser. If the winner gets x% of the votes, the loser gets (100 − x)%, making the margin exactly (2x − 100)% of the total valid votes.
